en: The Philippine eagle, scientifically known as Pithecophaga jefferyi, is the national bird and one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world.
Jose Rizal wrote the novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the injustices of the Spanish colonial government in the Philippines.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, serves as the highest judicial branch of the government.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago by carving stepped fields into the mountains of the Cordilleras.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño through a vibrant street dance featuring two steps forward and one step backward.
Dr. Fe del Mundo created a bamboo incubator for rural areas without electricity, significantly reducing infant mortality rates in the Philippines.
The Waling-waling, scientifically named Vanda sanderiana, is an orchid species endemic to Mindanao and is widely considered the queen of Philippine flowers.
The Barasoain Church in Malolos, Bulacan, served as the seat of the First Philippine Republic and the drafting site of the Malolos Constitution.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog but incorporates vocabulary and grammatical structures from other indigenous Philippine and foreign languages.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution guarantees the right to free public elementary and secondary education for all Filipino citizens.
National Artist Juan Luna painted the famous historical artwork Spoliarium, which won a gold medal at the Madrid Exposition of Fine Arts in 1884.
